lines.trans: Here are your croutons, cream, and carrot.
Great, and where is the fresh onion?
Here is the onion, start boiling the soup.
I will make the most delicious cream soup.
The main thing is do not oversalt the broth on the stove.

lines.trans: Do not worry, I know the exact recipe.
First chop the onion and carrot finely.
I will cut the vegetables into even pieces.
Then add butter and warm cream.
Everything will be ready on time, Senya.

lines.trans: I will come and check your dish.
You will be pleasantly surprised by this soup!

meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: clear liquid soup made by boiling meat or vegetables

examples.trans: The broth is simmering quietly on the stove.

examples.text: Главное, не пересоли бульон на плите.
examples.trans: The main thing is do not oversalt the broth on the stove.

examples.text: Бульон уже сварился для этого соуса?
examples.trans: Has the broth already boiled for this sauce?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

варить.gloss: to boil, to cook, to brew

meanings.en: to boil, to cook, to brew
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to boil', forming an aspectual pair with 'сварить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: We are cooking soup for lunch.
He brews very tasty coffee.
Then make coffee faster.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.
What delicious tea!

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

вовремя.gloss: on time, at the right moment

meanings.en: on time, at the right moment
meanings.note: 'не вовремя' = at a bad moment. Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'время').

examples.trans: Bad timing!
He always comes on time.

examples.text: Ну как же ты не вовремя! Где ты сейчас?
examples.trans: Your timing couldn't be worse! Where are you now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.

examples.trans: Don't worry.
I'm nervous.
Don't worry, I won't.

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There, look.
Here's my toy car.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Where's my toy car?
Where's Dad?

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').
Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
This is the main street.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)

examples.trans: I'm ready!
Lunch is ready.
Right, I'm ready!

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'бавить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to add', forming an aspectual pair with 'добавлять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to append') (to say in addition) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я просто хотел добавить яркий аромат.
examples.trans: I simply wanted to add a vivid aroma.

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

examples.text: Затем добавь масло и тёплые сливки.
examples.trans: Then add butter and warm cream.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, after that' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Затем мы подпишем все официальные документы.
examples.trans: Then we will sign all official documents.

examples.text: Затем добавь масло и тёплые сливки.
examples.trans: Then add butter and warm cream.

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.trans: As you all know...
I don't know.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: smooth soup made with pureed vegetables or cream

examples.trans: The chef prepared a cream soup.
I will make the most delicious cream soup.

meanings.note: Diminutive of кусок. Common masculine noun meaning 'slice, little piece, bit' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: May I have another slice?
Eat a slice of cake.

examples.text: Можно ещё кусочек? И шампанское можно выпить?
examples.trans: May I have another slice? And can I drink the champagne?

meanings.note: Also bow for archery. Common masculine noun meaning 'onion' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Onion, salt, pepper — and that's all.
Chop the onion for the salad.

examples.text: Попробуй! Лук, соль, перец — и всё.
examples.trans: Try it! Onion, salt, pepper — and that's all.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'butter', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Add a piece of butter to the pan.

examples.text: Затем добавь масло и тёплые сливки.
examples.trans: Then add butter and warm cream.

examples.text: Добавляем немного сливочного масла и соли.
examples.trans: We add a little butter and salt.

meanings.note: Там мелко = It's shallow there. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: What do you mean drowning? It's shallow there!
Near the shore it is very shallow.

examples.text: А чего тону? Там мелко! Сиди!
examples.trans: What do you mean drowning? It's shallow there! Stay put!

meanings.note: colloquial for морковь; also figuratively an enticing reward

examples.text: И в конце нас всех ждёт вкусная морковка!
examples.trans: And at the end a tasty carrot is waiting for us all!
There is fresh carrot in the soup.

examples.text: У нас есть взрослая цель — морковка.
examples.trans: We have a grown-up goal: the carrot.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'carrot', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Fresh carrot is lying on the table.

examples.text: Сначала мелко нарежь лук и морковь.
examples.trans: First chop the onion and carrot finely.
What difference does it make who cuts carrots?

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'резать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to slice', forming an aspectual pair with 'нарезать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to carve') (to slice meat or bread) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Вот теперь кусочки нарезаны красиво и аккуратно.
examples.trans: Now the pieces are cut beautifully and neatly.

examples.text: Сначала мелко нарежь лук и морковь.
examples.trans: First chop the onion and carrot finely.
I will cut the vegetables into even pieces.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.trans: When do I start?
The lesson starts at nine.

examples.text: Аркаш, ну что скажешь? Когда начинать?
examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: plant or part of plant used as food

examples.trans: Fresh vegetables are very healthy.

examples.text: Там мне дают только чистить овощи.
examples.trans: There they only give me vegetables to peel.
Chop fresh vegetables for the salad.

meanings.note: Used as an exclamation of approval. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya!
The suit fits you great.

examples.text: Отлично, Ваня! Вот это твой образ!
examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya! That right there is your look!

пересолить.gloss: oversalt, put too much salt in

meanings.en: to oversalt, to add too much salt
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'солить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'oversalt', forming an aspectual pair with 'пересаливать'.

examples.trans: Do not oversalt this broth.

examples.text: Главное, не пересоли бульон на плите.
examples.trans: The main thing is do not oversalt the broth on the stove.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'stove', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('slab') (large flat stone or concrete block) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Внимательно смотри за температурой на плите.
examples.trans: Watch carefully the temperature on the stove.

examples.text: Я сниму сковороду с горячей плиты вовремя.
examples.trans: I will remove the pan from the hot stove on time.

examples.text: Ладно, включай плиту и доставай мясо!
examples.trans: All right, turn on the stove and get the meat!

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

meanings.note: On foot, once. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.
I'll come tomorrow.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: очень приятно = pleased to meet you

examples.trans: Pleased to meet you.
It's nice here.

examples.text: Очень приятно. А в чём дело?
examples.trans: Pleased to meet you. So what's the matter?

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to check, to test', paired with 'проверять'.

examples.trans: Check the soldering iron.
We'll check everything right now.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву. Паяльник проверь.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood. Check the soldering iron.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'recipe', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Шеф хранит свой тайный рецепт супа.
examples.trans: The chef keeps his secret soup recipe.

examples.text: Да? Это мой старый фирменный рецепт.
examples.trans: Really? This is my old signature recipe.
Before you is a unique ancient recipe.

meanings.note: Without bumps or crooked edges. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('even, smooth, straight').

examples.trans: And your joints are even!
The road here is smooth and wide.

examples.text: И стыки у тебя ровные! Пока, Даня!
examples.trans: And your joints are even! Bye, Danya!

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
It's the biggest town.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Food, air, news. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вежий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fresh').

examples.trans: Fresh berries on the table.
I bought fresh bread.

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
I'll do it tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: fatty part of milk, used in cooking, plural-only noun

examples.trans: Pour warm cream into the soup.

examples.text: Вот твои сухарики, сливки и морковка.
examples.trans: Here are your croutons, cream, and carrot.

examples.text: Затем добавь масло и тёплые сливки.
examples.trans: Then add butter and warm cream.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'начала').
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'начала').

examples.trans: First they were rude and insulting over there.
Let's start everything from the beginning.

examples.text: Мы танцевали. Сначала они там грубили, оскорбляли.
examples.trans: We were dancing. First they were rude and insulting over there.

meanings.note: Hot liquid dish. Borrowed from French 'soupe' in the Petrine era.

examples.text: Сегодня на кухне сварили вкусный суп.
examples.trans: Today in the kitchen they cooked delicious soup.
I like hot soup very much!

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

meanings.note: toasted or dried bread piece used in soups or salads

examples.trans: Add croutons to the cream soup.

examples.text: Вот твои сухарики, сливки и морковка.
examples.trans: Here are your croutons, cream, and carrot.

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is your coffee.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
Your boss is here.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('exact, precise').

examples.trans: An exact answer.
Nobody knows the exact answer.
Wait, is this information accurate at all?

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Having a moderate degree of heat. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('warm').

examples.trans: And where are your warm gloves?

examples.text: Да, его тёплая шапка лежит прямо здесь.
examples.trans: Yes, his warm hat is lying right here.

examples.text: Снимайте скорее с него тёплые валенки.
examples.trans: Take off his warm felt boots quickly.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'surprised' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: The guest was pleasantly surprised.

examples.text: Ты будешь приятно удивлён этим супом!
examples.trans: You will be pleasantly surprised by this soup!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
